statement: The points $A(1,2)$, $B(4,6)$, $C(-2,3)$ form a triangle. (i) Find the equation of the line through $A$ perpendicular to $BC$. (ii) Find the area of triangle $ABC$. (iii) Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. (iv) Show that the same area is given by $\tfrac12\,|BC|\,d$, where $d$ is the perpendicular distance from $A$ to $BC$, and verify it equals $\tfrac{15}{2}$.
solution: (i) Gradient of $BC$ is $\frac{3-6}{-2-4}=\frac12$, so the perpendicular gradient is $-2$. Through $A(1,2)$: $y-2=-2(x-1)$, i.e. $y=-2x+4$. (ii) Area $=\frac12|1(6-3)+4(3-2)+(-2)(2-6)|=\frac12|3+4+8|=\frac{15}{2}$. (iii) Line $BC$: $y=\frac12 x+4$. Intersect with $y=-2x+4$: $\frac12 x+4=-2x+4\Rightarrow x=0$, $y=4$. Foot is $(0,4)$. (iv) $|BC|=\sqrt{(4+2)^{2}+(6-3)^{2}}=3\sqrt{5}$. Line $BC$ is $x-2y+8=0$, so $d=\frac{|1-4+8|}{\sqrt{1+4}}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{5}}=\sqrt{5}$. Then $\frac12|BC|\,d=\frac12\cdot 3\sqrt{5}\cdot\sqrt{5}=\frac{15}{2}$, agreeing with (ii).
hints: Compute the gradient of BC first.
Use the shoelace formula for area.
